get.description: The elections that are over and the ones the user voted in, with the user's own situation in each.
The bulletin board: every ballot of the election, public, so that anyone can check them (see app/utils/audit.py).

Is this receipt on the bulletin board of this election? Exactly this code: not one that contains it. Public, like the board it reads.
A receipt is 256 bits drawn at random: it cannot be found by trying, and it says nothing about who voted or what.
What is needed to check the count of a finished election against the bulletin board. Public, like the board.

AdminUserResponseModel.title: AdminUserResponseModel
AdminUserResponseModel.description: What the administrators of the users see of an account (never the password hash).

BinaryZKProofModel.title: BinaryZKProofModel
BinaryZKProofModel.description:
A non-interactive zero-knowledge proof (Cramer–Damgård–Schoenmakers OR proof, Fiat–Shamir) that a Paillier ciphertext
encrypts 0 or 1, without saying which. Numbers are decimal strings, because they do not fit a JSON number.

content.title: Content
content.description: Homomorphically encrypted ballot, with its proofs (JSON)

unique_code.title: Unique Code
unique_code.description: Unique code for the bulletin, used for verification

VoteAuditModel.title: VoteAuditModel
VoteAuditModel.description: What anyone needs to check the count of an election with the bulletin board (see app/utils/audit.py).

VoteCastData.title: VoteCastData
VoteCastData.description:
A ballot: for each candidate, an encryption of 0 or 1 with the proof that it is one of the two, and a proof that
the sum of all of them (the product of the ciphertexts) is 0 or 1 too: at most one candidate. Without that second proof,
a voter could encrypt a 1 for every candidate, and each one would pass.

VoteCreatorModel.title: VoteCreatorModel
VoteCreatorModel.description: Who created an election, as the voters see it: a name, never an email address or a phone number.

VoteResponseModel.title: VoteResponseModel
VoteResponseModel.description:
An election as the API shows it. The table model must never be a response: it holds the encrypted private key of the election
(and would hold anything added to the table later).
